# The EXACT Firebase class descriptors present in the release APK, measured from the built
# artifact of android-v0.10.1 (dex, 6 files, 54,404,248 bytes) and pinned here.
#
# WHY EXACT CLASSES AND NOT PACKAGES. The first version of this allow-list permitted whole
# packages — `components`, `encoders`, `events`, `inject` — which meant a new executable class
# added inside one of them, say `com/google/firebase/components/PushClient`, would have been
# waved through as "inert" while FirebaseApp stayed absent. Review caught that: a package-level
# allow-list is a weaker guard than the blanket ban it replaced, in the one direction that
# matters. So the set is exact, and anything not in it is red.
#
# WHAT THIS SET IS. Google's generic dependency-injection container (Component, ComponentRuntime,
# ComponentDiscovery, CycleDetector, Lazy, EventBus), its value/JSON encoder library, two
# injection interfaces, one marker annotation, and three exception types. The `Registrar` names
# are the container's own component discovery, not push registration. There is no push client, no
# network client, and no FirebaseApp — the class that initialises Firebase at all — which is
# asserted separately and is the premise that makes any of this inert.
#
# WHEN THIS GOES RED. A transitive dependency bump that adds or renames a class will fail the
# release check with the new descriptor named. That is correct: re-read what arrived, satisfy
# yourself it is still inert, and add the line. Do not replace this file with a prefix.
